items.title: Joseph "Red" Clark Interview, 1959-11-11
items.q: So Clitto, that's Marshall for the young men, he said, well, they got the body in charge, they're going to leave.

ctx.x: Well, how do you decide which organization has the body in charge?

Well, I don't know how they run that, you see. That's kind of complicated to me. When I go there and I bring my band to where I'm going to work. Well, they go there and then when they come out, say, well, we got this body in charge, we're going to leave. Sometimes they say, well, they're going to take it. And then we're going to take it. And then we're going to take it. It's like that funeral we got ahead over there last year sometime. Over the Vidoc down there around Wagner Street. I don't know if you remember…

What, back to going from the hall or wherever you meet the corner to the pick up the body, what kind of music would you play before you get to where the body is? Play hymns. Only hymns. That's right. Yeah. Nothing. But then fast tempo. That's right. Fast march. It should take time. Yeah. So you're with the body. You've picked up the body, either the church or the home or the undertaker, wherever it was. What would you play then?
